what: Re-opening cells only ever merges regions: flood the freed cells and fold every region they touch into the largest one (relabel only the smaller regions' cells) instead of re-running the 40k-cell labelling; closing cells can split regions, so it keeps the full relabel, batched once per reset
evidence: break nav update 5.8 ms (full labelRegions) -> 0.02-0.26 ms (mergeOpened); tests/unit/destruct.test.ts compares the incremental labels with a forced full relabel (same partition); reset of all 8 destructibles 15 -> ~5-9 ms with batchNavBlockers
rule: Make the frequent direction of a connectivity change incremental and prove it equal to the full recompute in a test

what: Breakable props merged into the static-prop style buckets can still toggle individually: record each prop's index range (and crease-segment range) at build time, hide by zeroing its indices (degenerate triangles) and parking its ink segments far below the world, show by copying the saved ranges back, then upload with addUpdateRange
evidence: src/client/world/destruct-view.ts: 8 destructibles standing + rubble in 3 meshes + 1 LineSegments2; a break costs ~0.17 ms of CPU and no geometry rebuild (tests/unit/destruct-perf.test.ts, destruct-view.test.ts checks the same index buffer object)
rule: For rare visibility flips inside merged geometry, rewrite index ranges instead of splitting draw calls or rebuilding buffers

what: A blast that breaks a wall must not also pass through it: destructibles take explode() damage in a listener that runs AFTER the characters were hit (their line-of-sight rays still see the wall), and the line of sight to the destructible itself must exclude its own colliders or the prop shields itself
evidence: src/sim/combat/projectiles.ts addBlastListener() call at the end of explode(); src/sim/destruct/damage.ts blastReaches() casts with a filterPredicate that skips the prop's own colliders; the cover test: a mortar just outside the garage wall leaves a tuna stack 2.7 m inside at full hp
rule: Order destructible damage after character damage in the same blast, and exclude the target's own colliders from its LOS ray

what: A Vite dev server started with watch: null (no-HMR, to keep other lanes' edits from reloading the page mid-screenshot) also never invalidates its transform cache: edits made after start are silently NOT served, so screenshots show stale code
evidence: artifacts/x1/x1-wall-debris.png was identical before and after the word-offset/scorch-color fix until the lab's Vite was restarted
rule: Restart a no-watch dev server after every code change before taking proof screenshots

what: A telegraph that starts in one system (paint event at order 150) and counts down in a later-ordered system of the same tick (tracking at 455) is one tick short: the sniper fired 1.083 s after the paint with a 1.1 s track, and 0.833 s with the 0.85 s phase-2 track
evidence: boss-sniper telegraph test: expected 1.0833 >= 1.0833333333333335 (paint→hit), fixed by not accumulating tracked time on the paint tick
rule: Count warning time from the tick after the warning event, and assert warning→damage ≥ the full telegraph (1e-6 tolerance), not ≥ telegraph − 1 tick

what: The sniper's laser dot is rebuilt by clients from lens(pos, yaw, pitch) + aim × distance (distance in the spare `ammo` field, cm). Aiming yaw/pitch from the pivot at the aim point and then drawing from the laterally offset lens put the drawn dot up to ~0.2 m off at 50 m; solving the aim so the ray from the lens passes through the aim point (3 fixed-point steps) and firing along exactly viewDir(yaw, pitch) makes the drawn dot the true impact
evidence: model muzzle vs sim lens 0.58 m before calibration, 6 mm after (tests/unit/boss-avatar.test.ts); boss-sniper test: the dot sits on the target before every hit
rule: When a telegraph is reconstructed client-side, put its origin + direction in one pure shared function and make the authority's hit test use exactly that ray; calibrate the origin against the model's muzzle in a test

what: check-boundaries greps src/sim for /\bwindow\./ even inside comments: 'before the recover window.' in a doc comment failed BOUNDARIES
evidence: BOUNDARIES: src/sim/boss/sniper.ts:46: /\bwindow\./ -> /** A shot's flash … before the recover window. */
rule: In src/sim, src/host and src/shared write 'beat'/'span' instead of ending a sentence with 'window.' (or 'document.')

what: A scripted human stand-in (sees only what a player sees: the dot on itself, the beam, the glint, the warning circles; 0.25–0.6 s reactions, greed when a shot is nearly charged, 0.28° aim error, a death costs 15 s) gave a believable boss duel length; deaths drive the variance (2–7 deaths → 125–242 s over 8 seeds). A harness bug that left the respawned marksman standing at the base in the sniper's view produced 27 deaths and a 'lost' fight
evidence: tests/unit/boss-sniper.test.ts duel(); SNIPER_SWEEP sweep: 125–242 s solo, 62–107 s with 3 L3 bots
rule: Balance bosses against a perception-limited stand-in, report a seed sweep (not one seed), and park the stand-in out of play while it is 'running back' after a death

what: A lab dev server started with server.watch.ignored ['**/*'] kept serving the first transform of labs/boss.ts: edits never reached the screenshots; and killing the npx pid left the node child holding the port, so the 'restart' died with EADDRINUSE while the stale server kept answering
evidence: curl of /labs/boss.ts still had the old camera line; vite-e1.log: httpServerStart error
rule: For a private no-HMR lab server keep file watching on (hmr:false only), start node node_modules/.bin/vite directly (kill that pid), and curl a changed line before trusting a screenshot

what: Stealth level design: pups told to hang back at the rally point still perceive at 45 m (clear weather). One that sees a sentry opens fire, the gunfire noise alerts every sentry in earshot, and the human's sneak is over before it starts. Chapter 2's first start was 36 m from a sentry: the alarm went off on the first live tick with the human hidden (conceal 1.0)
evidence: tests/unit/adventure-chapters.test.ts 'a still human hidden in the meadow…' failed until the start moved to 56 m from the nearest sentry (sentry loop 5 m + rally zone 4 m < 45 m margin)
rule: Keep every stealth rally point > sight range + sentry loop + rally radius from each sentry (or behind a wall); test it with a hidden human and hanging-back bots

what: The sim can move and turn a human's character (adventure relocation to the chapter start), but until the client's first input arrives the Room repeats PlayerSlot.lastCmd, whose yaw is the team spawn's from join. Movement copies input.yaw into e.yaw, so the snapshot showed the old facing and the client's localSpawn adopted it (the player faced the house, not the objective)
evidence: [localSpawn] yaw -2.234 (team spawn) vs -0.83 (chapter start) until the Room synced lastCmd.yaw on spawn events (docs/handoff/A1.md §3.3)
rule: When the authority places a player, sync the Room's held input (lastCmd yaw, mx/mz) too; e.yaw alone is overwritten by the next held input

what: New menu UI used short class names (.ch, .ch-grid…) and collided with U1's chat CSS (.ch …) inside the shared #cvc-hud root: the chapter cards got 380 px grid columns and absolute positioning, the grid overflowed the card and hid its header
evidence: artifacts/a1-menu-picker.png before/after renaming to .mm-chap-*; computed style showed grid-template-columns 380px 380px 380px and an extra zero-size .ch element (the chat)
rule: Prefix every class a lane injects into the shared HUD root with a lane-unique namespace (mm-chap-, cvc-adv av-), and grep hud-style.ts + other lanes' CSS before picking one

what: Headless SwiftShader pages stall for seconds (shader compiles, 1–2 fps): a DOM caption timeline on performance.now() jumped straight to its end and closed before one screenshot, and an authority clock started at worker boot ran most of a 7 s briefing before the first frame. Pacing captions by the frame dt the game loop already caps (0.25 s) and holding the briefing until a human joins (≤ 10 s) fixed both, and also helps slow real machines
evidence: a1-intro.png empty on 3 tries (3 caption lines 864 ms after the panel opened, then closed); with dt-paced captions + briefing wait the panel shows 2–3 lines
rule: Time presentation sequences with the capped frame dt, not wall clock; don't start authority-side presentation timers until the viewer is connected

what: Perception (AI, order 100) reads e.conceal written by the conceal system (order 620) on the previous tick: a test that teleports a corgi into tall grass on the same tick a sentry spawns gets it spotted at 31 m with 'conceal 1.00' printed a tick later. Real play never teleports into grass, so the fix belongs in the test (place during the briefing)
evidence: dbg: 't=7.0 ALERTED Tabby 1 target=Rex conceal=1.00' on the go-live tick; passes when Rex is placed one second earlier
rule: In stealth tests, move the target into cover at least one tick before any observer can perceive it

what: V8's Math.hypot allocates a FixedDoubleArray on every call. The audio engine's distanceTo and the footstep speed used it per entity per frame; the engine-loop manager's first cut allocated ~400 B/update from hypot alone
evidence: HeapProfiler sampling with includeObjectsCollectedByMinorGC/MajorGC: 20 MB of samples under hypot in 50k updates → 0 after Math.sqrt(dx*dx+dy*dy+dz*dz) (tests/unit/audio-vehicles-alloc.test.ts, docs/handoff/S2.md)
rule: In per-frame code write Math.sqrt of the squared sum, never Math.hypot

what: A computed double passed as an argument to a function V8 does not inline is boxed into a 12-byte HeapNumber per call. Knob.to(v, now), voice.set(P, now) and steer(..., now, step) left ~40 B/update after every object allocation was gone
evidence: S2 loop manager: 1.9 → 0 B/update once per-update doubles moved into fields / a Float64Array target bank flushed in one loop; the remaining bytes were the computed intensity argument into update() and the duck's setTargetAtTime binding
rule: For zero-allocation hot paths keep per-update doubles in object fields or typed arrays and pass objects, not doubles; count Web Audio binding calls (which always box) separately

what: The V8 sampling heap profiler reports only objects still alive when sampling stops, so per-frame garbage is invisible by default. A heap-growth test in a file shared with other tests measured 16 B/update where the same code measured 0.05 B/update alone: other tests' polymorphic use of the fakes changed V8's inlining
evidence: tests/unit/audio-vehicles-alloc.test.ts: heapUsed delta with 0 GCs (PerformanceObserver 'gc'), harness baseline subtracted, 40k updates: 0.05–0.13 B/update in its own file vs 16 B/update inside audio-vehicles.test.ts
rule: Profile garbage with startSampling({ includeObjectsCollectedByMinorGC: true, includeObjectsCollectedByMajorGC: true }); run byte-exact allocation tests in their own test file (fresh process) and subtract a harness baseline

what: Listening by numbers with no speakers: OfflineAudioContext.suspend(t) (at render-quantum multiples) drives per-frame manager code inside an offline render, so scripted scenes (a kart accelerating, a plane flyby, 4 loops stacked) render deterministically in headless Chromium. Raw RMS misjudged the loop-vs-transient balance: the first kart voice read −18 dBFS RMS, above a Squeaker shot, and most of it was a 10–36 Hz firing fundamental that would pump the master compressor
evidence: docs/handoff/S2.md §3: K-weighted (BS.1770-style) levels, 2–3.5 kHz band power vs a footstep, envelope depth and autocorrelation rate per segment; a 70 Hz high-pass on the kart and a lower plane low-pass took the plane's footstep-band energy from +16 dB over a footstep to 7 dB under
rule: Balance continuous loops against transients with K-weighted short-term levels and band power in the footstep/shot bands, not raw RMS; high-pass sub-audio engine fundamentals

what: The chapter's last step emits score 'step', 'chapter' and 'win' on the same tick, and a vehicle rider is Grounded with the vehicle's velocity, so the footstep system played a running patter for every kart driver
evidence: src/sim/adventure/runner.ts completeStep → enterStep → completeChapter; src/sim/vehicles/common.ts seatCharacterAt sets Mounted | Grounded; S2 tests 'the chapter tick plays the fanfare alone' and 'a seated rider makes no footsteps'
rule: Defer a per-step stinger one frame so a same-tick finale can replace it, mute the generic sting while the finale plays, and skip EFlag.Mounted in anything driven by character locomotion

what: Breacher bots in a destroy step planted a Dig Charge 3.4 m from the breach wall's ANCHOR (A1's test) but 2.8 m from its box, just outside X1's 2.6 m breaching reach, so it sat on its 30 s fuse; their 'no own charge' rule then blocked a second, correct plant for the whole 30 s (the wall fell 32 s after the squad arrived)
evidence: src/sim/ai/tactics.ts chargeFits(): destructDistance(def, feet) <= BREACH.reach - 0.5, and only an own charge already within reach of that prop blocks a plant; approachProp() walks to the face nearest the bot. Chapter 3 bot-only: breach step 32.3 s -> 2.7 s (seed 1)
rule: Measure 'close enough' to an object by the same geometry its rule uses (the prop's boxes), not its anchor point; a cooldown/ownership guard must be scoped to the target it protects

what: A headless harness that reads room.pendingEvents after room.tick() misses the events of every snapshot tick: sendSnapshots() replaces the array every other tick, so ability counts came out 1 instead of 7
evidence: scratch play harness vs tests/unit/adventure-a2-chapters.test.ts (wraps sim.drainEvents to see every event)
rule: To observe a Room-driven sim's events, wrap sim.drainEvents (the Room drains it once per tick), never the Room's outgoing buffers

what: A scripted jump that toggles Jump every tick (press, release, press) gets the release-early cut (vel.y x0.5) on the second tick, so a stand-in 'jumping' off the garage roof just fell; the double jump also needs a released tick before the second press
evidence: src/sim/systems/movement.ts (jumpHeld && !jumpHeldNow halves vel.y); tests/unit/adventure-a2-yard.test.ts leapOffTheRoof holds Jump while vel.y > 1, releases one tick, holds again, then Q at the second apex
rule: Scripted human stand-ins hold buttons the way hands do (hold through the rise, release before a re-press); verify a traversal claim with the stand-in, not with the bot waiver

what: A barricade raised for the human by the chapter emitted `ability squeak_barrier` with the human's id: the HUD started the human's own Q cooldown ring (it showed 11 s) although the sim cooldown was untouched
evidence: src/client/ui/hud.ts ability case (ev.id === localId); screenshot artifacts/a2-porch_siege-barricades.png before/after; src/sim/adventure/props.ts now emits on the wall's id (X1's kiosk-vend precedent)
rule: World or scripted effects that reuse a class ability's event must carry the object's id, not a player's: clients read `ability` events with a player's id as that player's own ability

what: Featured-kit steps (a Skyraider glide, a roof perch, a plane) are human-only rules that bots can't meet: A1's bot-only waiver keeps headless runs completable, and a fail-forward grace (120 s on one step, then the rule relaxes with a pup bark) keeps a human with the wrong kit or no skill yet from a soft-lock, without making the kit optional for anyone who can use it
evidence: src/sim/adventure/runner.ts strictRules / STRICT_GRACE_SECONDS; tests/unit/adventure-a2-yard.test.ts (a double jump or an Assault lands short of the glide zone; a gliding Skyraider completes it at 6.5 m up) and adventure-a2.test.ts (grace)
rule: When a step demands a kit or a vehicle, pair the strict rule with a timed fail-forward, and prove the strict rule with a scripted stand-in on the real map

what: Bot-only chapter runs can't catch 'bots steal the human's step': with a human in the squad, Breacher pups escorting ch3's reach step next to the breach wall planted C2's hold-zone Dig Charges (zoneGoal sets t.hold for reach escorts), X1's breaching fuse armed them, and the wall blew 5.5 s after go-live, so the human's 'blow the wall' step completed 0.02 s after arriving (4/4 seeds)
evidence: tools/qa-adventure.mjs steal; src/sim/ai/tactics.ts:499 (zoneGoal hold=true) + :253 (hold-zone charge); src/sim/destruct/damage.ts breachCharges; docs/qa/W4_VERIFICATION.md P1-1
rule: Every chapter needs one run with a human slot that idles: nothing a later step owns may happen before that step is live

what: Checking whether a featured kit matters: re-running bot-only chapters with every pup set to one kit (sim.state.adventureConfig.chapter.pups) separated the hard gates (ch3 breach, never finished without Breachers) from kits that only look featured (ch2/4/5/6 finished in the same time with four Assaults)
evidence: tools/qa-adventure.mjs offkit vs bots --seeds 7
rule: Prove a 'kit matters' claim with an A/B that removes the kit, not only by showing the kit at work

what: A teleported stealth stand-in was 'spotted' on the first tick while hidden in tall grass: e.conceal is written by the world system (order 250) after the AI (100) has already perceived, so the stale 'open' level applied for one tick
evidence: tools/qa-adventure.mjs stealth (sets e.conceal like the world system after placeCharacter); src/sim/ai/brain.ts perceive() concealLevel
rule: After placeCharacter in a stealth test, set the concealment the world system would compute (or walk the stand-in in) before judging detection

what: Fail-forward needs its own difficulty check: forcing a squad wipe on a checkpoint step and counting re-wipes against natural arrivals showed the Porch Siege's last wave re-wiped in 5/8 seeds after a restart vs 0/8 on first arrival, which the lanes' bot-only runs (never wiping) could not show
evidence: tools/qa-adventure.mjs wipe --chapters porch_siege --at 3 vs bots; artifacts/q2/logs/porch.log
rule: Measure the retry, not just the first attempt: a checkpoint restart must not be harder than arriving at the step

what: Two SwiftShader pages on 4 shared cores: the second client's first frame blocked its main thread past the server's 30 s idle timeout and it was kicked (4000) mid-join; the same test passed with both pages at 480x270 while loading, resized to 1280x720 only for screenshots. Separately, a screenshot taken right at an adaptive pixel-ratio step can come back as the page background
evidence: tools/qa-w4online.mjs; artifacts/q2/logs/prod.log ('c17 closed: idle timeout'); artifacts/q2/blank-frame-laser_dawn-run1.png
rule: Load headless multi-client tests at a small viewport; record canvas size and frame index with every screenshot before calling a blank frame a render bug

what: A character rising along a wall can read as grounded mid-jump (the controller touches the edge); a jump controller that let go of Jump on 'grounded' triggered the release-early cut and halved the jump, so cats never cleared the lean-to -> roof step
evidence: src/sim/ai/nav-links.ts legStep holds Jump while vel.y > 0.8 whatever grounded says; the cat's west-route leg 5 went from FAIL to landing (tests/unit/ai-nav-links.test.ts validation, 6 profiles)
rule: Scripted jumps key the release on vertical velocity, not on the grounded flag

what: surfaceAt(x, z, maxY) returns the highest top at or below maxY even when something solid sits on it: a deck flood with a 0.5 m step walked from the roof onto the parapet body (7.68) under its cap (7.8), and over a stack of shingles onto the 0.5 m-wide parapet top
evidence: src/sim/ai/nav.ts buildDeckGrid: reject a cell when a surface within 1.2 m sits above the one found, or when a footprint corner (+-0.25 m) drops away; the roof deck test asserts every cell < 7.55 m and inside the walls
rule: A walkable-surface test checks the whole footprint and what sits on the surface, not one point's top

what: Hop links are validated with the exact controller the bots run (legStep), per movement profile, in a scratch Rapier world of the static props near the links plus a cropped terrain grid, stepping stepCharacter + stepWorldEffects WITHOUT world.step(): a static world and a controller that skips its own collider need no broad-phase refresh, which was 2/3 of the tick cost; ~2.6 k ticks = 45-100 ms per profile
evidence: src/sim/ai/nav-links.ts scratchFor/scratchTick; tests/unit/ai-nav-links.test.ts replays every validated link in a real Sim (movement + world + physics step): every leg lands
rule: Validate traversal with the shipped controller and prove any simulation shortcut by replaying the result in the real Sim

what: The ground path follower passed a waypoint from up to 0.8 m away and headed for the next corner on a line that clipped the trampoline's cylinder collider, where Rapier's character controller deadlocks (zero velocity even pushing along the wall); the random detour then walked straight back into it: a Warden was stuck 5.0 s in the TDM soak
evidence: src/sim/ai/brain.ts steerOn (pass a waypoint only when the next one is straight-line walkable from the bot) + the stuck detour (wedged in a closed cell: nearest open cell first); soak stuck max TDM 5.0 -> 1.5 s
rule: A follower may only cut to the next corner when the straight line from where it actually stands is walkable; recovery moves must also be straight-line reachable

what: Arrive-style braking in the air killed the horizontal speed a bot needed to clear a parapet or reach a lower ledge; steering airborne legs by timed arrival (horizontal speed = remaining distance / time until the fall reaches the target's height, full speed while still below the target) made every drop and descent land, and walking off a ledge needs a minimum stick when the point sits at the wall's foot
evidence: src/sim/ai/nav-links.ts legStep steering; drops went from 1/6 to 5/6 landing, both route descents validate for all 6 profiles
rule: Steer jumps and falls by time-to-land, not by stopping distance

what: A checkpoint restart rebuilt the squad in a tight formation around the rally anchor. At the Porch Siege that anchor sits behind the porch, so the restarted pups had no sight lines to the last wave (they dealt 236 damage in 12 s vs 800 on a natural arrival). Two pups could share one spot when every ring candidate failed and all fell back to the same nearest walkable cell. The respawned brains also start without targets while the cats don't.
evidence: porch_siege forced wipe at step 3: seed 3 looped 8 wipes; 15 seeds re-wiped 3/15 (13 later wipes) → 1/15 (2) after restoring each member's step-start spot plus a 2 s regroup beat (cats stunned); first attempts unchanged
rule: A checkpoint restores the squad where it stood when the step began (validated, formation as fallback, never two on one spot) and gives the respawned side a short regroup beat, so a retry is never harder than the first try.

what: The adaptive pixel ratio (setPixelRatio → canvas resize → clear) ran after ctx.render() in the same frame, so a cleared back buffer could reach the compositor: a blank frame at each resolution step.
evidence: Q2 saw 3 of 6 first-run chapter screenshots solid background at ~frame 30 (the first adaptive step); moving quality.update before render removes the window
rule: Anything that resizes the canvas runs before the frame's render, never between render and present.

what: The soak's net-bot is a Room 'human' driven by a combat brain; in adventure, reach steps wait for the human, so the soak never left step 1 and reported open-ended results as fine. Its bandwidth was JSON.stringify of the undelta'd message (90-100 KB/s) instead of the wire.
evidence: adventure soak: 'matches 0 (wave 1)' → chapter 1 complete at 44-65 s bot-only; TDM snap 94 KB/s raw vs 9 KB/s through SnapEncoder
rule: Soak each mode the way it is really played (bot-only squads where a human would gate progress) and measure bandwidth through the same encoder the server sends.

what: The room setup accepted any well-formed chapter id; the sim silently fell back to chapter 1 while /rooms listed the bogus id, so the browser advertised a chapter the room wasn't playing.
evidence: ?chapter=nonexistent listed as-is while Yard Day ran; after resolving ids against CHAPTERS at the server edge the listing shows Yard Day
rule: Resolve untrusted ids to the value the authority will actually use at the edge (sanitize to the real default), so every view of the room agrees with the sim.

what: A kart's velocity lags its nose by the grip slip (yaw rate / grip, ~10 degrees), so a ram run that steered the nose at the target hit 0.8-1 m off centre and dealt 25-57 instead of ~90.
evidence: logged contact geometry: lateral miss 0.45-1.0 m with nose steering; 0.05-0.2 m after steering the direction of travel onto the intercept point
rule: When a vehicle must arrive somewhere precisely (a ram, a gate), steer its velocity vector, not its heading.

what: worldLineClear() uses WORLD_RAY_FILTER, which includes vehicles: a sight line started at a plane's (or kart's) own center hits its own hull, so every dive check failed and the bot pilot never attacked.
evidence: 0 dives in 30 s of TDM sorties; starting the ray (radius + 0.3 m) toward the target gave 3 dives and gun hits at once
rule: Start rays from a vehicle just outside its hull (or pass the collider to exclude); check what a shared ray filter contains before reusing it.

what: A look-ahead 'terrain ahead' check that included the dive's own planned descent pulled every strafing run out at ~13 m, while the dive-entry check allowed the dive: the plane dove and aborted in a loop, never firing.
evidence: pull-out reason 'ground ahead' at 13-14 m AGL on every dive; checking only props rising above the lawn in the look-ahead (the AGL floor handles the ground) and using one clearance for entry and abort gave 8 dives and 22 rounds in 40 s
rule: Entry and abort conditions of a maneuver must use the same model and thresholds; predictive checks should look for obstacles, not for the maneuver itself.

what: Bots engaged with a kart's rider back straight off from it at run speed (the brain keeps its preferred range), so even dead-centre rams close at only ~12 m/s and deal ~55-60, not the 94 a head-on boosted ram promises.
evidence: at contact: kart 17-18 m/s along the normal, target 5-6.2 m/s away along it (tn); dmg 51-63 on 140-160 hp targets; ram kills 2 in 4 x 180 s matches
rule: Measure the target's reaction before tuning an attack's payoff: the 'ram pays' estimate uses the target's current speed away, and target choice prefers pets facing elsewhere.

what: Sim outcomes depend on what ran earlier in the same process: a 45 s TDM Room before a bot-only chapter 6 changes its step times (47.3 -> 47.4 s, then 233.4 -> 216.9 s), with or without the B2 brain hook; back-to-back identical runs still agree.
evidence: npx tsx b2-leak.mts twice (A == B) vs tdm-then-ch6 on the committed tree (no B2 hook); the divergence starts in step 2, after the flying
rule: Keep per-world caches free of per-sim state (validation, stamps, scratch); test determinism across a different preceding sim, not only a repeat.

what: three's WebGPURenderer RenderObject subscribes to the 'dispose' event of its object, material AND geometry. A transient mesh that shares a cached geometry or material and is merely removed from the scene stays referenced from that shared resource's listener list, with its render objects and per-object uniform buffers, for the life of the page.
evidence: 10-min headless TDM: +188 WebGLBuffer, +157 RenderObject, +166 NodeUniformsGroup in 5 min (heap snapshot diff); dispose-listener counts on the shared drone geometry grew +18 per 3 min; after dispatching 'dispose' on dropped subtrees: none
rule: When a view leaves the scene, dispatch {type:'dispose'} on every object of its subtree (engine/release.ts releaseObject3D), even when geometry and materials are shared and must survive.

what: A per-view registry that is only appended to (ability views kept every ink LineSegments2 ever created for a later resolution update that never came) pins whole dead views through .parent.
evidence: retainer paths: abilityViews → inkLines[n] → LineSegments2 .parent → Mesh → Group; 78 dead meshes per 5 min → 0 after removing the unused array
rule: Find leaks by heap snapshot retainer paths, not guesses; never keep a list of scene objects without removing entries when the object leaves.

what: Measuring 'no memory growth' needs a forced GC before each sample and a slope after warm-up; JIT code alone adds ~0.15 MB/min for the first minutes of a session and tapers, so a short run's slope overstates a leak.
evidence: client heap slope 0.25 → 0.19 → −0.001 MB/min (least squares from 60 s) across the two fixes; code:code was +750 KB of a 5-min diff
rule: Judge growth by what the heap diff names (meshes, buffers, render objects), and by the late-session slope, not by the raw first-to-last delta.

what: Assigning a new geometry to a live mesh in three's WebGPURenderer (r186) is not clean: RenderObject.setGeometry swaps the reference but leaves its 'dispose' listener on the OLD geometry and adds none to the new one, so a shared old geometry keeps the render object alive and the new geometry's dispose never reaches it.
evidence: node_modules/three/src/renderers/common/RenderObject.js setGeometry() vs the constructor's addEventListener + dispose()'s removeEventListener on this.geometry; C3 swaps a new SkinnedMesh instead: 111 in-place look swaps x 2 avatars in the lab kept renderer.info.memory.geometries flat at 11-13, 0 errors
rule: To change what a live character wears, replace the mesh object (new SkinnedMesh bound to the same Skeleton, re-parent the bone root, then dispatch 'dispose' on the old mesh via releaseObject3D) instead of assigning mesh.geometry.

what: A cosmetic that must fit a nearly full triangle budget (hero kit 5,970 / 6,000) can pay for itself by replacing what it covers: every neckwear drops the team collar + tag from the body variant (102 hero / 72-80 NPC triangles freed), so any look stays in budget without touching K1's tuned geometry.
evidence: worst kit with any look 5,996 / 6,000 hero (corgi overwatch + bow tie), 3,475 / 3,500 NPC; neckwear 92-128 tris each; tests/unit/cosmetics-looks.test.ts audits every coat x class x team x tier and every neckwear x class x breed x tier
rule: Before raising a budget for an add-on, find the part it replaces and build a body variant without it (cache key + 1 flag).

what: Keeping a look to paint (coat = vertex colours) and never letting it change the body shape (the seed keeps the breed) makes 'silhouettes unchanged with any look' true by construction and testable by array equality, instead of re-running a perceptual metric per look.
evidence: a test asserts identical position / index / skinIndex arrays between every coat body and the classic body; K1 class distances with every neckwear moved <= 0.002 (closest pairs 0.133 / 0.136 unchanged)
rule: Separate what a player may change (paint, one accessory) from what carries gameplay reads (silhouette, rig); make the cache key show the split.

what: Parallel lanes share the session scratchpad directory: another lane's same-named helper script (shots.mjs) was run with my arguments and created a DIRECTORY at the PNG path I asked for, so later screenshots failed with EISDIR.
evidence: navigating to "60?webgl&quality=low" in the error; artifacts/c3/iter2-coats.png existed as an empty directory
rule: Put scratch scripts in a lane-named subfolder of the scratchpad (scratchpad/<lane>/) and never assume a scratch file you wrote earlier is still yours.

what: A new menu view's root class `lk` (locker) collided with the pause overlay's existing `#cvc-hud .lk` rule (absolute, inset 0, grey veil, centred grid): the locker rendered under a veil with centred tiles. Every HUD rule lives in one scoped stylesheet, so short class names collide silently.
evidence: artifacts/p2-profile: first locker shot showed the veil; grep of hud.ts/hud-style.ts listed lk-main/lk-panel/lk-settings…; after renaming to the `lo-` prefix the view rendered correctly
rule: Before adding a view to hud-style.ts, grep the stylesheet and hud.ts for the class and prefix you plan to use; give each view its own unused prefix.

what: Entrance animations that start at opacity 0 with a delay and fill-mode both (LEVEL UP!, NEW LOOKS! on the reward card) were still invisible 2.6 s after show in one headless scene and visible in another: on a starved frame clock (SwiftShader, ~1 fps) delayed animations lag, and the essential text stays hidden.
evidence: reward-chapter-720.png (first take) had no LEVEL UP / NEW LOOKS badge; reward-match-720.png taken the same way had both; switching to scale-only pops (never opacity 0) showed them in every take
rule: Never hide essential UI behind a delayed opacity-0 entrance; pop by scale (or animate without a delay) so the content is readable from the first frame.

what: Two local stores record the same event: A1's chapter card writes the gold paw to cvc.adventure a moment before the profile records the match, and the profile's load folds cvc.adventure in and evaluates unlocks. The medal look was therefore already unlocked in the 'before' profile, and the reward card never announced it.
evidence: reward-chapter-720.png listed 4 new looks without the Spiked Collar (gold paw: The Garage Job); tests/unit/profile-content.test.ts 'recordMatch after the chapter card saved the paw' failed before the fix, passes after
rule: When recording an event that another writer may already have persisted, build 'before' from your own store only, apply the event, then merge the other source; test with the other writer going first.

what: Playwright's click() waits forever on an element with aria-disabled="true" (it counts as not enabled), so a locked-but-focusable locker tile made the e2e time out although the page behaved correctly.
evidence: tests/e2e/locker.spec.ts: 45 × 'element is not enabled' retries on [data-look=corgi_sable]; focus() + keyboard Enter passes
rule: For controls that stay focusable but refuse (aria-disabled, not disabled), drive them in e2e the way keyboard and pad players do: focus() then press Enter.

what: three r186 caches node-material programs by type + node children only (NodeMaterial.customProgramCacheKey). Overriding setupLightingModel on a MeshToonNodeMaterial INSTANCE would silently share a program with plain toon materials that have the same nodes; per-material JS numbers baked into the shader would do the same.
evidence: HardenedToonMaterial: subclass with static type 'HardenedToonNodeMaterial', detail/surfaceAttr/puddle appended to customProgramCacheKey, rough/metal/grime/wear/mud/fade/wetK read with materialReference; tests/unit/style-hardened.test.ts asserts two materials differing only in weathering values share one key and detail/attr/puddle do not
rule: A new lighting model = a subclass with its own static type; per-material scalars go through materialReference (shared program, per-material uniforms); compile-time switches go into customProgramCacheKey.

what: An additively blended decal with the default fog = true draws a lit rectangle over its whole quad: fog mixes the (zero) additive colour toward the fog colour, so fog is ADDED where the decal should add nothing.
evidence: S4 floodlight pools: a pale parallelogram around the pool at the center bookmark (artifacts/s4/iter/i1-high-clear-center.png) gone with poolMat.fog = false (artifacts/s4/iter2)
rule: Additive FX materials set fog = false (fade them by distance in the shader if needed); only normally blended FX take scene fog.

what: Wet look without an env map: wetness lowers roughness only to a sheen (rough * 0.55 + 0.08) and darkens porous albedo; near-mirror roughness is reserved for a puddle mask on flat up-facing parts, and the sky reflection dims with storm darkness. A uniformly glossy wet lawn mirrored the pale horizon at grazing angles and read as snow.
evidence: artifacts/s4/iter3/high-storm-deck.png (snow-like sheet, wet rough 0.14 + 0.16r) vs artifacts/s4/iter5/high-storm-deck.png (dark wet lawn, puddle 0.32, env stormDim 0.55)
rule: Keep mirrors in masks (puddles, metal), give everything else a sheen; judge wet surfaces at grazing angles, where Fresnel makes mistakes obvious.

what: With several lanes editing one tree, a shared Vite dev server full-reloads the page mid-capture (window.__lab undefined halfway through a shot batch), and before/after numbers drift as other lanes' work and new commits land.
evidence: S4 before-shots died after 8/10 bookmarks; HEAD moved 657cc7a -> 1dc3604 during the lane; perf compared on git-archive exports of the same HEAD with and without the S4 files: default view high 125/1.215 M vs 126/1.217 M, low 74/0.699 M both, live TDM 300/1.406 M vs 301/1.407 M
rule: Captures run on a private Vite with server.hmr=false and server.watch=null (restart it to pick up your own edits); render-cost before/after compares git-archive exports of ONE HEAD with and without your files.

what: Armour was paid for by culling geometry nobody can see: cranium triangles whose three corners lie inside the class headgear's cut (minus a 0.06 pi margin) are dropped before the merge, plus X-eyes as 4x2 diamonds, 3-sided rims/straps/belts and fewer rows on small caps (pupils, cheeks).
evidence: K2: corgi overwatch hero 5,970 -> 5,730 with plate carrier, armour collar, shoulder plates, knee pads, boots, bracers, team lamps and scars added; NPC max 3,427 -> 3,332; veterans hero <= 5,866 / NPC <= 3,418 (node tools/char-audit.mjs, tests/unit/characters-k2.test.ts)
rule: Before simplifying visible parts to fit new gear, cull what the gear hides (same cut function as the gear, with a margin) and trim segment counts on sub-pixel parts.

what: Common armour (the same plates on every class) and a global proportion change both shrink the K1 Jaccard class distances: adding shoulder plates pulled cat assault toward breacher (0.136 -> 0.125), and a 3.5 % smaller cat head lowered the warden cone so breacher/warden fell 0.16 -> 0.13.
evidence: node tools/char-silhouette.mjs --seed 1/3/13 during K2; fixed by keeping plates within ~3 cm of the body and enlarging the class signatures (taller breacher charges, wider warden cone flare): worst pair 0.122 -> 0.144, every seed and species above its pre-K2 value
rule: After any change shared by all classes, re-run char-silhouette for seeds 1/3/13 per species and restore distance by growing the class's own signature shape, never by shrinking the armour below readability.

what: Vertex-colour team markings one vertex row wide fail the team-read metric (and render as a soft gradient): each triangle's colour is the average of its corners, and crimson averaged with ochre turns orange (outside the 22 degree hue window) while blue averaged with ochre turns grey.
evidence: readability teamRead, K2: corgi assault on the cats team 3.0 % vs 5.1 % on its own team with the same 1-row pack band; 2+ row bands and whole shoulder shells in the team colour gave >= 6.2 % everywhere
rule: Paint signal areas across at least two adjacent vertex rows (or a whole part), and check both teams on both species with teamRead.

what: One weathered material for a whole character: MeshBuilder.surface([rough, metal, grime, wear]) writes the `surface` vec4 attribute that S4's toon({ surfaceAttr: true }) reads, so fur, cloth, armour, metal and wet eyes/noses share one draw. Any other mesh drawn with that material must carry the attribute too (the weapon now gets its own toon({ surface: 'weapon' })). Parts with metal >= 0.8 go near-black at dusk (diffuse x (1 - metal)), so brass buckles and rank insignia use a half-metal 'fitting' surface.
evidence: K2 lab close-ups artifacts/k2/iter6-close-*.png (full-metal gold crest read black) vs the final gallery; tests/unit/characters-k2.test.ts checks the attribute
rule: Tag every primitive with a surface when the body material reads surfaceAttr; keep coloured metal fittings at metal <= 0.5.

what: Under parallel lanes, a vite dev server with HMR reloads a capture page whenever ANY lane saves a file in its import graph (and once more when the dep optimizer finishes), so paused/armed lab state vanishes mid-capture.
evidence: X3 lab captures lost __wlab between frames (page reloaded); fixed with a private vite config (server.hmr=false, watch=null) restarted after my own edits, plus a capture script that re-arms a freshly loaded held page
rule: For screenshots under concurrent editing, run your own vite with hmr:false + watch:null on a free port, restart it after your edits, and make the capture script idempotent against reloads (start held, arm, release).

what: Particle/decal materials that write colour straight into colorNode receive palette hex as linear values, so sRGB palette colours come out washed-out (smoke and brass read near-white at dusk); toon materials don't show it because three converts their Color params.
evidence: X3 halftone smoke rendered light beige with PALETTE mixes; converting hex/255 with ^2.2 (a 256-entry table for the per-call glow colours) gave the intended grey and brass
rule: Linearize palette colours before writing them into custom TSL colour nodes (particles, decals); keep a lookup table so the hot path stays allocation- and pow-free.

what: Short FX spawned from network events arrive between frames and got aged by a full frame before their first render (a 70 ms flash was half gone at 30 fps); a per-particle 'fresh' flag that skips the first update makes the first rendered frame show t = 0, which is what lines a flash up with the sound played from the same event.
evidence: fx-weapons.test.ts: a spawned particle writes t = 0 after update(0.2) with freshFirstFrame; lab frame sequence shows the flash at full strength on the event frame
rule: Anything spawned from an event (not inside the frame loop) should skip its first integration step; age it from the frame it is first drawn.

what: A hitscan shot's impact read better when the sparks, the hole and the ricochet sound land when the tracer reaches the target (dist / tracer speed, capped at 0.3 s) instead of on the shot frame; a fixed Float32Array ring of pending impacts keeps it allocation-free and the audio engine takes the same delay on the audio clock.
evidence: lab OTS sequence: flash on frame 10, tracer + metal sparks + hole on frame 12 at 9.4 m; audio-weapons.test.ts checks the impact voice starts 'delay' later; firefight test: 1.65 B/shot heap growth over 4,596 shots
rule: Share one impactDelay(tracer, dist) between FX and audio so visuals and sound stay in sync by construction.

what: The terrain 'bowl' op is ABSOLUTE (the floor goes to -depth world height, the pond's design), so a crater stamped with it becomes a 1.4 m pit on a rise and a bump in a dip; relative stamps ('hole' for the dish + a ring of small 'raise' ops for the ejecta rim) give the same crater everywhere
evidence: E4 craters with bowl: centre-minus-surround depth 0.13 m at (-12.5,-16.5), 1.4 m at (29.2,15.5), -0.07 m (a bump) at (-15,-45.5); with hole+raise: 0.5-0.6 m everywhere
rule: Stamp local features with relative ops (hole/raise/path); use bowl/flat/pit only where an absolute height is the point

what: Hidden keep-outs for new solid props are scripted and straight-line vehicle routes, not only nav paths: A2's ch3 test drives the parked kart by pure pursuit straight from (81,-43) to the garden gate (-77,-63.5), and V1's 40 s random drive starts at (-30,-55); FOB crates on that line stalled the kart for 29 s and wedged the random drive at 90 m (needs 150)
evidence: E4: adventure-a2-yard escape 'live' not 'complete', vehicles-yard moved 89.8; after keeping a 3.5 m lane along the straight line and moving the armory: escape in 12.3 s, random drive 186 m
rule: Before placing solids, grep the tests for scripted spawn/drive coordinates and assert a clear lane along straight lines between parked vehicles and their goals

what: Chaotic bot statistics (ai-drive-brain 'rams >= 3 over seeds 1-3') flip with ANY world change; to tell a regression from chaos, copy the tree to the scratchpad with only your lane's files reverted (git show HEAD:path > copy; delete your new files; symlink node_modules) and run the same test on other seeds in both copies
evidence: E4: rams over seeds 1-3 / 4-6 / 7-9 = baseline 5 / 1 / 2, E4 world 1 / 2 / >=3; terrain-only and props-only variants also moved seeds 1-3 (1 and 0 rams)
rule: A/B a flaky threshold on several seed batches in a reverted scratch copy before redesigning content around it; report the batch numbers to the test's owner

what: D3-style collider==visual sampling (3x3 points at +-0.8 of the half extents) hits exact seams: two abutting boxes both miss a point on their shared face in float, and a thin plate leaning at 77 deg answers boxTopAt with a height on its slanted face where 1-cm-proud decals sit higher
evidence: E4 world-fortifications: 'visual top -Infinity' at sack joints and open-crate felt edges until the top-row sacks overlapped 2 mm and the felt 1 cm under the walls; the garden signs had to be excluded as non-floors
rule: Overlap standing-surface visuals by a millimetre at joints, and exclude plates steeper than the walkable slope from standing-surface tests
